```{r}
##Part A — Creating Vectors and List
##Question #1:
# 1. Create a vector for the worker's age
ages <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 
          35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 
          50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 
          35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 
          48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

# b. How many data points?
num_data_points <- length(ages)
num_data_points

# c. Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker's age
min_age <- min(ages)
max_age <- max(ages)
min_age
max_age

# d. Access the 13th to 18th elements and 33rd to 35th elements
subset_d <- c(ages, ages)
subset_d

# e. Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements
subset_e <- ages[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]
subset_e

# f. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0
ages[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
ages

##Question #2:
data(rivers)

# 1 & 2. Get stats and combine into one named vector
river_stats <- c(
  Length = length(rivers),
  Sum = sum(rivers),
  Mean = mean(rivers),
  Median = median(rivers),
  Var = var(rivers),
  SD = sd(rivers),
  Min = min(rivers),
  Max = max(rivers)
)
river_stats

##Question #3:
# 1. Create vectors according to Forbes ranking data
celebrity <- c("Oprah Winfrey", "Tiger Woods", "Madonna", "Elton John", "Tom Cruise", "J.K. Rowling")
power_ranking <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 18)
pay <- c(225, 100, 50, 48, 31, 75)

forbes_df <- data.frame(celebrity, power_ranking, pay)
forbes_df

# 2. Modify the power ranking and pay of J.K. Rowling to 15 and 90 respectively
forbes_df$power_ranking[forbes_df$celebrity == "J.K. Rowling"] <- 15
forbes_df$pay[forbes_df$celebrity == "J.K. Rowling"] <- 90
forbes_df

##Question #4:
# 1. Create a list of ten vegetables
veg_list <- list("Carrot", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Potato", "Tomato", 
                 "Cabbage", "Lettuce", "Cucumber", "Onion", "Garlic")
veg_list

# a. Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables in the list
veg_list <- list("Peas", "Corn")
veg_list

# b. How many datapoints do you have?
length(veg_list)

# c. Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5
veg_list <- c(veg_list[1:5], list("Bean", "Squash", "Celery", "Radish"), veg_list[6:length(veg_list)])
veg_list

# d. How many datapoints does your vegetable list have?
length(veg_list)


```
